_comment: Minecraft difficulty is a property of the WORLD - one value in level.dat for everything - so
this cannot be configured per dimension and is instead applied as you travel, on the
dimension change and re-checked once a second in case a command moves it.
WHY HARD IS THE MAJORITY, and it is mechanical rather than taste: a villager killed by a
zombie converts to a zombie villager 100% of the time on HARD, only sometimes on NORMAL and
never on EASY - and curing a converted villager is what grants the permanent trading
discount that a trading hall is built around. So every pocket dimension where a villager
The three on NORMAL are the ones whose premise fights a trading hall rather than the ones
that are meant to be easy: skyblock starts in the void, onechunk is a single 16x16 chunk,
and oneblock is one regenerating block. Hard buys nothing there and only punishes the
opening. Move any of them to hard freely - it is one word here.
The hub and redstone land are creative sandboxes, so PEACEFUL: no hostiles, no hunger.
A real dimension with no entry of its own INHERITS its pocket dimension's difficulty, so
hub:survival_nether follows hub:survival. List one explicitly only to differ deliberately.
Single player is the designed case. The setting is global, so with several players spread
across pocket dimensions there is only one value available; it follows whoever changed
dimension last. Remove an entry, or the whole file, to leave difficulty alone entirely.
